issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] STILL-OPEN SC-10(1) REGRESSION, site 1 (segment verb loop, __scan_one_segment_for_cp_delete ~line 2261). __mask_opaque_spans() computes the right answer but the very next line throws it away: the guard is `if [[ "$__STRIPPED" != "$__MASKED" ]]`, i.e. the verb list is consulted only when __strip_dollar_brace() ALSO changed something. For a token split by command substitution alone (no ${...}), masking yields the literal verb but __STRIPPED == __MASKED, so the loop is skipped and the residual `*'${'*` check is false too -> unarmed. Measured: `r$(true)m -rf .claude` -> allow, and in an isolated lab the .claude directory was ACTUALLY DELETED. Bisect: f36a921=ask, 133aa93=allow, 58d407a=allow -> this is the same 34th-verdict regression, not a new pre-existing gap. Sweep (5 verbs x 4 substitution forms x every internal split position x 3 control-plane targets) = 164/180 allow. Root cause verified on a scratchpad copy: changing the single comparand `$__MASKED` -> `$NORM_TOK` (the pre-133aa93 comparand) turns all probed payloads to ask while `ls $(pwd)`, `echo $(git rev-parse HEAD)` and the 15th-verdict declared residual `$(${Z:-r}${Z:-m} -rf .claude)` all stay allow.

[security][critical][confidence:high] STILL-OPEN SC-10(1) REGRESSION, site 3 (opaque-span scanner). __note_opaque_verb() (~line 1543) applies __strip_dollar_brace() to the span but was never wired to __mask_opaque_spans(), so a substitution nested inside a substitution/backtick span still hides the verb. Measured: ``` `f$(true)ind .claude -delete` ``` -> allow, `` `find .claude -dele$(true)te` `` -> allow, `$(f$(true)ind .claude -delete)` -> allow, `` `r$(true)m -rf .claude` `` -> allow. Isolated lab: `.claude/settings.json` and the `.claude` directory were ACTUALLY DELETED. Bisect: both find-form payloads were ask at f36a921 and allow at 133aa93 -> same regression class, still open. Direction (needs its own friction check, do not apply blindly): mask NESTED spans only, i.e. strip the outer $(...)/backtick wrapper first, then __mask_opaque_spans() the remainder. On `$(${Z:-r}${Z:-m} -rf .claude)` that remainder contains no nested span, so the 15th-verdict declared residual is preserved by construction.
